# Keep tooltips within screen bounds

## Problem statement

Tooltips are rendered at a fixed offset from the hover point without any viewport-bounds checking. When a hovered element sits near the right or bottom edge of the window, the tooltip overflows the viewport; in the DOM-rendered mode this extends the document's scrollable area, so the page "resizes to make space" (scrollbars appear / layout shifts). The tooltip must always be positioned so that it is fully visible and never alters the document layout.

## Users

- **Players** hovering cards, HUD elements, and buttons in Main Street, Lost Cities, Sushi Go, and the Gym tooltip/Gym-card-index demos.
- **Engine consumers (game developers)** who rely on the shared `TooltipManager` (DOM and Phaser modes) so they do not have to re-implement bounds handling per game.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I hover a card near the right edge of the screen, the tooltip appears fully on-screen instead of being clipped or pushing the page wider.
- As a player, showing a tooltip never causes the game canvas or page to jump/resize.
- As a game developer, when I supply a `phaserRender` callback I can clamp my tooltip into the game canvas with a shared helper rather than copying clamp maths between games.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **DOM-mode clamping:** For a hover point near each of the four viewport edges, the DOM tooltip's rendered bounding rectangle is fully inside the browser viewport (`left >= 0`, `top >= 0`, `right <= window.innerWidth`, `bottom <= window.innerHeight`), with a small margin. Verified by a browser (`*.browser.test.ts`) test in `tests/ui/`.
2. **No document resize:** Showing (and hiding) a DOM tooltip does not change the document scroll size — no horizontal/vertical scrollbar is introduced (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth` and `scrollHeight === clientHeight` before and after `show()`). Verified by a browser test.
3. **Phaser-mode clamping:** The shared Phaser render callbacks keep their tooltip containers inside the game canvas bounds (`0..GAME_W` × `0..GAME_H`) at all four edges. Gym's callback (currently unclamped) is brought in line with the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, ideally via a shared, unit-tested helper. Verified by unit tests (helper) plus the existing scene/browser tests.
4. **No regression to existing positioning:** Existing world→screen coordinate mapping (canvas scale, canvas offset, camera scroll) and the settings `showTooltips` toggle behaviour are preserved; the existing `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` / `TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` expectations are updated rather than weakened.
5. **Validation and documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (tooltip component section) and any relevant Gym help text. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies.
- Must not regress reduced-motion, `pointer-events: none`, or the maximum `z-index` behaviour of the DOM tooltip.
- Must remain safe in non-DOM environments (`document`/`window` undefined) and when the canvas bounding rect cannot be read — fall back to hiding, as today.
- Clamping must be cheap (measure once per `show()`, no per-frame layout thrash, no resize listeners).
- The DOM tooltip node must not contribute to the document's scrollable overflow area.
- Use UK English in comments and docs; escape only backticks in worklog content.
- Existing tests that assert `div.style.position === 'absolute'` will need updating if the positioning strategy changes (see Risks).

## Existing state

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — `TooltipManager`. DOM mode computes `screenX`/`screenY` from the canvas rect, camera scroll, and scale, then sets `left`/`top` = point + `(10, 10)` offset with **no bounds check**. The node is `position: absolute`, `pointer-events: none`, `z-index: 2147483647`, `max-width: 320px`, appended to `document.body`. Phaser mode delegates layout entirely to the caller's `phaserRender` callback.
- Consumers in DOM mode: Main Street (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` constructs it; `MainStreetRendererStreet/Hud/Market/Layout.ts` call `show`), `GymTooltipScene` DOM half, `GymCardIndexScene`.
- Consumers in Phaser mode: `LostCitiesScene.ts` (`createTooltipManager`) and `SushiGoScene.ts` — both already clamp with `Phaser.Math.Clamp(..., 4, GAME_W - boxW - 4)` etc. `GymTooltipScene`'s Phaser callback does **not** clamp.
- Tests: `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` (unit), `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` (browser, asserts `position === 'absolute'`), `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` (SLL anchors only), plus Main Street tooltip content tests.
- Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents `TooltipManager`; `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` maps the tooltip scenes.

## Desired change

- Add viewport-bounds clamping to the shared DOM tooltip renderer in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`:
  - Position the node relative to the viewport so it cannot extend the document scroll area (e.g. `position: fixed`).
  - Measure the node after setting content, then flip it above/left of the hover point when there is not enough room below/right, and clamp to the viewport as a final guard, keeping a small margin.
  - Keep the existing world→screen conversion (canvas rect + camera scroll + scale).
- Extract a reusable bounds-clamping helper for in-canvas (Phaser) tooltips, mirroring the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, and use it in `GymTooltipScene` (and optionally migrate Lost Cities / Sushi Go to the shared helper with no behaviour change).
- Add unit tests for the clamp maths (all four edges, both axes, oversized tooltip) and browser tests proving the tooltip stays in the viewport and does not change document scroll size.
- Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (and Gym help text if the scene behaviour/description changes).
- **Test-first:** author the clamp-helper unit tests and the browser edge/document-scroll tests before wiring the DOM renderer and the Gym callback, so the new behaviour is specified by failing tests first.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — Add DOM-mode viewport clamping / anti-resize positioning; export a reusable Phaser-mode clamp helper.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — Apply the clamp helper in the `phaserRender` callback (currently unclamped).
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` — Unit tests for clamp maths via the DOM mock and helper.
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` — Edge-position + document-scroll-size assertions; update the `position` selector assumption.
- `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` — Extend with Gym Phaser-mode in-bounds assertions (if the scene callback is changed).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Document the bounds guarantee for both tooltip modes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the correct, complete interpretation of the title is "no tooltip (in either DOM or Phaser mode) may render outside its visible bounds", not just the DOM overlay. The DOM mode is the cause of the reported page-resize; Phaser mode only clips. Recommended and assumed.
- **Assumption:** clamping (shift/flip to stay visible) is preferred over truncating content or shrinking the tooltip. Documented assumption; trivially revisitable.
- **Risk:** switching the DOM node to `position: fixed` invalidates the existing browser test's `position === 'absolute'` selector — update the selector to target the tooltip by its stable attributes (`pointer-events: none` + `z-index`) rather than `position`.
- **Risk:** measuring the node to clamp requires it to be laid out; setting `display: block` before measuring may cause a one-frame flash. Mitigate by measuring immediately after content is set and before paint (single synchronous reflow), or measure with `visibility: hidden` then reveal.
- **Risk:** `window`/`document` may be undefined in unit tests/SSR — guard clamping behind the existing `document` checks and fall back to the unclamped path (or hide) when dimensions are unavailable.
- **Risk:** double clamping when a game's `phaserRender` already clamps — the helper must be opt-in and not re-apply automatically to caller-managed containers.
- **Risk:** oversized tooltips (taller/wider than the viewport) cannot fit; clamp to the margin and accept partial visibility, documenting the behaviour.
- **Scope-creep risk:** tooltip content wrapping/truncation, touch/long-press tooltips, and tooltip theming are out of scope; record as separate work items if raised.

## Related work

- **CG-0MLW74R8B04GYNP7** – Implement tooltip display/hide on card hover (completed) — introduced the shared `TooltipManager` this bug affects.
- **CG-0MODIX70W002JXQN** – `feat(ui): add TooltipManager` / `fix(ui): DOM-positioned tooltip displays above cards` — prior DOM coordinate-mapping work in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`.
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed) — SLL precedent for declarative positioning.
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed) — SLL layout system; relevant if bounds handling is expressed via SLL zones.
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed) — Main Street tooltip content fix, no overlap with positioning.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed)
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ake, bounds, displayed, ensure, keep (+11 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+10 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+7 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q:** Are there open questions requiring producer input? — **A:** No. The seed context ("Sometimes when a tooltip is displayed it would render outside the screen bounds. This results in the screen resizing to make space. We need to ensure that the tooltip is positioned such that it stays within screen bounds.") plus repository research was sufficient to draft a clear, testable brief. No interview round was required. Source: seed context supplied with the intake invocation + repo inspection.

**Prior related answers:** none.

**Research summary:** Inspected `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` (DOM node is `position: absolute` on `document.body` with no bounds check — the resize cause; Phaser mode delegates to `phaserRender`), the four in-repo consumers (Main Street, Gym DOM, Gym Phaser, Lost Cities, Sushi Go), and the existing tests/docs. Lost Cities and Sushi Go already clamp inside the canvas with `Phaser.Math.Clamp`; Gym and the DOM renderer do not. No existing shared clamp helper exists. Related completed tooltip work items were found via `wl search` (see automated report).

## Goal

Resolve game-specific assets (thumbnails and other files) relative to each game's artifact directory, and serve them safely to the Electron renderer under a packaged `file://`/asar build — realising AC3 (asset resolution).

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). `GameSelectorScene` currently loads `assets/<thumbnail>.png` from the launcher's own `public/` root; runtime games must instead resolve from `<contentDir>/games/<id>/…`. Direct `file://` image loads from arbitrary content dirs can hit CORS/canvas-taint and path issues, so a scoped custom protocol is introduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Asset resolution** — Thumbnails and other game-specific assets are resolved relative to the game's artifact location (not relative to the launcher's `public/` directory).
- **Asset resolution** — A pure resolver `resolveGameAssetUrl(gameId, relativePath)` returns a `tce-games://<id>/<normalised-path>` URL, rejecting any path that escapes the game directory (`..`, absolute paths, `\0`).
- The Electron main process registers a `tce-games://` protocol (privileged/`standard` + `secure`) that resolves requests only inside `<contentDir>/games/`; requests outside that root return `404`/are denied.
- The protocol handler is Electron-free-unit-testable via an injectable file reader/resolver (no Electron import in the pure logic).
- MIME types are set for at least `.png`; unknown extensions are served as `application/octet-stream`.
- Unit tests cover the resolver (valid, traversal, encoded traversal) and the protocol path-resolution logic.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `src/ui/game-asset-url.ts` with `resolveGameAssetUrl` + `resolveAssetFilePath(contentDir, requestUrl)`.
- Register the protocol in `electron/main.ts` before window creation (`protocol.handle`), reusing the resolver.
- Tests in `tests/ui/game-asset-url.test.ts` and `tests/electron/game-protocol.test.ts`.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/game-asset-url.ts`
- `electron/main.ts`
- `tests/ui/game-asset-url.test.ts`
- `tests/electron/game-protocol.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 loader test harness & fixture.

## Goal

Render the merged static + dynamic catalogue in the Game Selector identically, and surface incompatible runtime games to the user as a non-blocking notice.

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). Realises AC1 (dynamic games appear alongside static ones) and AC4 (incompatible games hidden, presence noted). Producer decision (this session, Q2 = A): incompatible games are **hidden** from the grid and listed in a notice line.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GameSelectorScene` renders dynamic entries through the same card-layout code path as static entries; a game loaded at runtime with a thumbnail renders it using its resolved `tce-games://` URL.
- Incompatible games are absent from the card grid and listed in a visible notice (e.g. `Incompatible game: X — requires core vY.Z`), using SLL/`anchorPoint`-based positioning (no new hardcoded pixel coordinates).
- A dynamic game whose thumbnail fails to load degrades gracefully (text-only card, no exception) — extending the existing `hasThumbnail` guard.
- An empty dynamic catalogue (no `games/` dir) leaves the selector pixel-identical to the current static-only behaviour.
- A browser test covers: merged static+dynamic rendering, the incompatible notice, and missing-thumbnail degradation.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `GameEntry` with optional `incompatible?: { requiredRange: string }` (or pass a separate `incompatibleGames` list into `init`/registry).
- Add a `renderIncompatibleNotice()` helper to `GameSelectorScene` and route thumbnail URLs through `image.setTexture`/loader using already-resolved URLs.
- Browser test in `tests/ui/game-selector-plugin.browser.test.ts`.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts`
- `tests/ui/game-selector-plugin.browser.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F4 dynamic ESM import & scene registration.

## Problem statement

The Tableau Card Engine ships pre-1.0 builds (currently `v0.1.17`), but nothing in the UI signals that players are using an ALPHA build. Every game screen, the game-selector menu, and the Help/Settings panes should show a brightly coloured red **ALPHA** badge carrying the current version number, so users and testers always know they are on an unreleased ALPHA build.

## Users

- **Players / testers** — "When I open any game, I can immediately see that this is an ALPHA build and which version I'm on, so I know to report issues and can quote the exact version."
- **Release manager / producer** — "I can visually confirm from any screen that the deployed build is an ALPHA build and that the running version matches the release."
- **Developers** — "The badge is rendered by one shared helper, so adding a new game scene automatically gets the ALPHA banner with no per-game work."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A bright red **ALPHA** badge displaying the current version string (from `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`, i.e. the build-time `__APP_VERSION__`) is rendered **stacked above/over the title** on every Example Game scene and every Gym demo scene, delivered through the shared scene-title helper (`createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()`), so no per-game bespoke code is required.
2. The same red ALPHA + version badge appears stacked above/over the one-off title on the Game Selector menu screen.
3. The SettingsPanel title shows the badge stacked above/over it, and HelpPanel gains a compact **"Help" + ALPHA badge** header at the top of its content (HelpPanel currently has no title heading).
4. The badge's version text equals `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`; the existing muted version labels on the menu (top-right) and settings (bottom-left) remain unchanged.
5. The badge renders correctly (legible, no clipping, no overlap with the Menu button or HUD controls) at the supported Game Selector canvas sizes; automated tests cover the shared badge helper and assert the badge is created on each surface.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Shared-helper first.** All scene/game/Gym titles already route through `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()` (`src/ui/SceneHeader.ts`); extend those rather than patching individual scenes. The Game Selector title, `SettingsPanel` title, and `HelpPanel` header are separate one-off call sites.
- **Reuse the version source.** Do not access `__APP_VERSION__` directly — import the existing `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` / style constants from `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` so version handling stays in one place.
- **No new assets / permissive only.** Red badge must be drawn with Phaser primitives (rectangle + text); no new image assets, no new dependencies.
- **Do not remove existing version labels** (producer decision Q3a) — the badge is additive.
- **Reduced motion.** The badge is static (no animation), so it is inherently reduced-motion safe; do not add motion.
- **Canvas headroom.** Scene titles sit at `SCENE_HEADER_Y = 14`; a badge stacked *above* the title has little vertical room. Option (c) permits overlaying/overlapping the title's upper edge; the chosen geometry must remain legible and must not collide with the top-left `Menu` button or top-right HUD controls.
- **SLL requirement.** Positioning must respect the project's SLL/no-hardcoded-pixel rule where practical; the title helpers already own their fixed header geometry, so the badge should be defined relative to the title it decorates.

## Existing state

- `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` — `createSceneTitle()` (centred title at `GAME_W/2`, `SCENE_HEADER_Y = 14`) and `createSceneHeader()` (title + `Menu` button). Used by all Example Game renderers/scenes and `GymSceneBase.initHeader()`.
- `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` — `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` (`v<version>` from build-time `__APP_VERSION__`), `VERSION_COLOR`, `VERSION_ALPHA`, `VERSION_DEPTH`, `createVersionLabel()`.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — one-off bold title `'Tableau Card Engine'` at `(GAME_W/2, 30)` with a subtitle; version label already rendered top-right below the GitHub icon.
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — one-off `'Settings'` title at `(panelWidth/2, PADDING + 30)`.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — sections rendered in a scrollable content container; **no** title heading today.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSceneBase.ts` — `initHeader(title)` delegates to `createSceneHeader()`.

## Desired change

Add a shared `createAlphaBadge(scene, opts)` factory (in `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` or a new `src/ui/AlphaBadge.ts`) that renders a bright red badge containing `ALPHA` and `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`, positioned stacked above/over a given title (with an explicit anchor/y so callers control overlap). Wire it into `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()` by default (with an opt-out flag) so every Example Game and Gym scene inherits it, then add it explicitly to the Game Selector title, the SettingsPanel title, and a new compact HelpPanel header. Keep the existing muted version labels.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` — Add `createAlphaBadge()`; render the badge from `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()` (default on, opt-out config).
- `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` — Reuse `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`; add red-badge style constants (or a `createAlphaBadge` export here if it fits better).
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — Stack the badge above/over the `'Tableau Card Engine'` title.
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — Stack the badge above/over the `'Settings'` title.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — Add a compact `Help` + ALPHA badge header at the top of the content area.
- `src/ui/index.ts` — Export the new badge factory/constants.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSceneBase.ts` — Verify the inherited header path renders the badge (likely no change if `createSceneHeader()` handles it).
- `tests/ui/*.test.ts` / `*.browser.test.ts` — Unit/integration tests for the badge helper and per-surface presence.

## Related work

- `CG-0MR89YKN0000FK5W` — Add game version to menu screen and Main Street settings panel (completed) — established the version-label pattern this item extends.
- `CG-0MSHQPDQ80015RF7` — Move the version number on the menu page below the GitHub logo (completed) — current version-label placement.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — top-of-canvas clipping.** Stacking a badge above a title at `y = 14` risks clipping at the canvas edge or colliding with the `Menu` button. *Mitigation:* define the badge geometry relative to the title with a small controlled overlap (per option (c)), and verify at supported canvas sizes; add a browser test/visual check.
- **Risk — banner overload.** Adding a badge to *all* surfaces (Q2a) could add visual noise to 30+ Gym dev scenes. *Mitigation:* keep the badge compact and consistent; it is intentional per the producer decision.
- **Risk — duplicate version indicators.** Existing muted labels plus the new badge duplicate the version on the menu/settings. *Accepted* per Q3a (badge is reinforced, not consolidated); noted as intentional.
- **Assumption —** `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` is always available in scenes (it already is, via build-time `define`).
- **Assumption —** the Game Selector title has enough headroom above `y = 30` to stack a badge; if not, the badge may overlap the title's top edge (permitted by option (c)).
- **Scope-creep risk.** Temptation to restyle other HUD chrome or remove the muted version labels. Record such opportunities as linked work items, do not expand scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Context gathered before asking: all menu/game/Gym titles route through `createSceneTitle()`/`createSceneHeader()` (`src/ui/SceneHeader.ts`), the menu title is a one-off in `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts`, the settings title is in `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, and `HelpPanel.ts` has no title heading. The version string already exists as build-time `__APP_VERSION__` (`src/ui/versionDisplay.ts`, currently `v0.1.17`).

- **Q1 — Visual form and placement of the ALPHA banner?**
  Options: (a) inline red pill badge to the right of each title; (b) full-width red ribbon at the canvas top; (c) red badge stacked above/over the title. Agent recommendation: (a) — keeps the title as the anchor and avoids covering HUD buttons.
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (c)** — red badge stacked above/over the title.

- **Q2 — Which surfaces receive the banner?**
  Options: (a) every title (GameSelector, all example games, all Gym scenes, Help + Settings); (b) game and menu titles only; (c) menu + Help/Settings only. Agent recommendation: (a) — item says "all game screens".
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a)** — every title, including Help and Settings headers.

- **Q3 — Help/Settings pane treatment and existing version labels?**
  Options: (a) badge on SettingsPanel title + compact "Help" + ALPHA header on HelpPanel, keep existing muted version labels; (b) SettingsPanel only; (c) remove the existing muted version labels. Agent recommendation: (a) — covers both panes while preserving existing labels.
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a)** — SettingsPanel + compact HelpPanel header; keep existing muted version labels.

Round 1 was originally raised by the `intake` skill on 2026-09-26 (comment `CG-C0MUIFEVBM006J5DY`) and flagged `needsProducerReview`; the producer answered all three questions in this session.



## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSVM3WCD007BRQP** – Synergy lines drawn edge-to-edge / corner-to-corner instead of center-to-center (completed)
- **CG-0MTIILDBB001F01S** – Competitive Monte Carlo harness: head-to-head simulation (blocked)
- **CG-0MLV6G3NO0OIUBZO** – Splendor card/token/noble type definitions and data (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: add, along, alpha, banner, current, game, games, help, menu, number, red, screens, settings, should, string, title, version
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: add, along, alpha, banner, current, game, games, help, menu, number, red, screens, settings, should, string, title, version
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md` — matched: add, along, current, game, games, help, menu, number, red, settings, should, string, title, version
